chapter: Looking back and the New York years
title: Owning a home and working for himself
summary: Smith says he has done better in Dallas, owns his home and works carpentry and roofing when he feels like it.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: So ...(?).... I've done better here than I did running all up and down the road in them big band times. I got to meet a lot of people here and I started to buy me a home. I couldn't do it when I was on the road, running around with them big bands. I started buying this old rat trap here. I need to fix it up now. I've been here twenty years or better.
Yeah. I've never done nothin' to it.
Do you like the fact that you're active now, and you're doing all this carpentry and roofing and mending cars...?
Or would you rather be retired and sitting at home?
I'd rather be doing what I'm doing, I think. I've got to get around and do a little something every now and then.

Yeah. I like that. And I'm working for myself. I can do a little fishing when I get ready, go down there and stay down in the water. That's the reason why I've got this little truck with the camper on it. Somebody broke into it and stole $200 worth of tools -- the glass and screen cut back there. Yeah, it's sitting right there in the yard. They broke in there and they stole all my (?) tools except that big power saw to cut lumber with -- I've got two or three of them back around here. I couldn't get them in that box. That's the reason they didn't get those.
So in other words, I just work when I feel like it.
